responses.evidence: B-01 and B-02 now name one composition. B-01 states the list contract on the parameter itself: writingStageIds holds only the stages that actually changed the tree, in the order they ran, so a stage that ran and left the tree byte-identical contributes no id — which is why production's noopPostApprovalWritingStage (src/final-evaluation.ts:67) never appears and why a committed cleaner's id is last even though the cleaner runs first (:42-48). B-02 rebuilt to match: CLEANER_STAGE_ID when cleaner.ran && cleaner.outputTreeId !== cleaner.inputTreeId, then POST_APPROVAL_WRITING_STAGE_ID only when currentFinalTreeId !== stageInputTreeId, so the committed-cleaner case is exactly [CLEANER_STAGE_ID] and the last-id rule names the cleaner. The three places now agree on that case: the test-plan bullet asserts stageId "cleaner" for [CLEANER_STAGE_ID] (and "post-approval-writing" for the two-id list, which is correct because the injected stub wrote last), the manifest's B-01 observableResult asserts the three stageId values for the three lists, the manifest's B-02 observableResult keeps S3 seeing the RESTORE handled by the cleaner branch, and the DoD line now reads 'passes only the stages that changed the tree they were handed, in run order, so [CLEANER_STAGE_ID] is the committed-cleaner list under production's no-op stage and a RESTORE then names cleaner' rather than the unfalsifiable earlier wording. B-03's re-dispatch, B-04's revert and EXHAUSTED record, and S3's 'the restore route names cleaner' are therefore reachable on a faithful implementation. A new unit bullet pins the list builder's three outputs directly.

The stage-duration event does exist and is written to events.jsonl. src/run-events.ts:347-371 declares the RunEventPayload member { type: "stage-duration"; ghIssue; sliceNumber?; agent; round?; durationMs; history; ratioToMedian? } — the explorer's grep missed it because the member is spelled with the literal type string, not with a field named elapsed or roundsSpent. It is emitted by RunJournal.observeStageDuration (src/run-journal.ts:133-168), which appends the line after pairing each phase-ended with the newest unmatched phase-started under stageInvocationKey (src/stage-durations.ts:57-63); src/run-journal.test.ts:663-733 and src/qa-orchestration.test.ts:2926-2945 both assert those lines on real streams, and src/run-snapshot.ts:410-412 skips them by name. The agents this slice needs are already carried: src/orchestrator.ts:6862 and :6928 emit the cleaner's phase-started/phase-ended with agent: "cleaner", and :7559 the final evaluator's with agent: "evaluator-final". PRD D11 (prd.md:550-555, :569-573) names exactly this source: 'Per-stage elapsed time = stage-duration events with agent: "cleaner" / "evaluator-final"' and 'model time (sum of stage-duration.durationMs)'. Dropping the column would therefore have contradicted the PRD rather than fixing a gap. The finding's underlying request is met instead: B-09 now cites src/run-events.ts:347-371 and src/run-journal.ts:133-168 and states the matching key — ghIssue plus agent, with agent === "cleaner" for stage "cleaner" and agent === "evaluator-final" for stage "final-evaluation" — plus the missing-phase-ended case (model ms 0); B-10 names B-09's sum as the column's source; the test-plan bullet seeds stage-duration lines for both agents and asserts the summed model ms and the 0 case; and the stage-durations non-goal is rewritten to say the file is not edited while its events are read, which is the same posture every other src/logger.ts reader takes toward the stream. No event kind is invented and no source is silently substituted.

The directory segment is no longer pinned; only the stem is. B-13 now states the archived file as the name cleaner-log-r<generator-round>-a<cleaner-round>.log (src/artifacts.ts:772) inside whatever directory the caller passes as archiveCleanerLog's archiveDir — the reviewArchiveDir value src/orchestrator.ts:6968 already holds, under .afk/artifacts/<run-slug>/slice-<n>/ — and says explicitly that the segment beneath that prefix is not pinned because the builder composing it lives in the out-of-scope src/artifacts.ts. The verification that archiveDir is the caller's own value is direct: src/artifacts.ts:758-767 takes archiveDir as a parameter and passes it through to archiveEvidenceCopy, and src/orchestrator.ts:6962-6972 supplies reviewArchiveDir. The S3 bullet and the DoD line follow: both now pin the stem cleaner-log-r1-a3.log with r1 = first generator round and a3 = third cleaner round, and both say the directory is resolved from the run's artifact tree rather than hard-coded. The manifest's B-13 then/observableResult carry the same split, so a correct implementation cannot fail the DoD on a directory detail the declared evidence never reached.

The Scope lock now carries an ordering note as a recorded decision: the restore re-dispatch and revert path (B-01-B-05, B-12) lands first because it is what #97 AC1 asks for and what the merge behavior depends on, then the ROI evidence family (B-06-B-11, B-13). It states that the two halves share exactly one seam — the cleaner round's own evidence, from which B-07's emission and nothing else is derived — and that each half is independently green on its own tree, so the ROI half is independently shippable and is the separable one if the session runs short.
